text.p: These are the leading stories in Sarajevo press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories nor does it vouch for their accuracy.

- United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees presented the final document on return of refugees in 1997 in Geneva on Wednesday. About 50,000 minority refugees are expected to return to 17 Bosnian towns, according to the document.
- Seventeen generals and two brigadiers sign first professional military contracts with the Moslem-Croat federation army.

- Newspaper sources say the Soros Foundation, a major donor in Bosnia's post-war reconstruction, will soon cease to finance an independent television network TVIN, founded by international community last September to counter local televesion's biased reporting.
- The international community continues to express outrage at the trial of seven Bosnian Moslems in Serb town of Zvornik, calling the proceedings a "farce" and "travesty".
- The Bosnian Serb parliament holds seventh session without Serb president Biljana Plavsic on Wednesday. After five hour-long discussion, deputies adopted the basis for economic policy in 1997.
- Thanks to donations provided by Italian humanitarian organizations, Sarajevo's Kosevo hospital becomes the only institution responsible for AIDS treatment in Bosnia and Herzegovina.
- The Japanese government allocated 3.9 billion yen for the reconstruction process in Bosnia and Herzegovina in 1997, newspaper says.
- Rasim Kadic, minister for refugees and displaced persons in Moslem-Croat federation says that seventeen towns within the fedration are ready for minority returns of 50.000 people.
- An international commission, charged with registrating request for the return of Brcko refugees begins operating in the Bosnian federation part of the disputed town.

- Fikret Abdic, a renegade Moslem leader and Hrvoje Sarinic, chief of staff in the office of Croatian President Franjo Tudjman met in Zagreb behind closed doors. They reportedly discussed Abdic's plan on resettlement of Moslems from Croatia to Velika Kladusa, newpaper sources said. -- Sarajevo newsroom +387-71-663-864
